title: Development and Evaluation of a Measurement Paradigm for Studying Cortical Language Processing in Cochlear Implant Patients
summary:
The goal of this study is to develop a simple and reliable measurement method that can be used to investigate how the brain processes speech. The study focuses on people with a cochlear implant (CI), which is a hearing aid for people with severe hearing loss.

To this end, the brain’s responses to various speech sounds are measured using small electrodes placed on the scalp. The study investigates which speech sounds and which electrode positions are particularly well-suited for these measurements. In addition, a more complex measurement system is compared with a simpler device that can also be used in everyday clinical practice.

Adults with normal hearing as well as people with cochlear implants are participating in the study.
The results are intended to help better assess speech processing in people with cochlear implants and to enable more efficient hearing diagnostics.
conditions: Cortical speech processing in cochlear implant patients

interventions.name: Participants with Cochlear Implant will take part in a one-time session involving tone audiometry, simultaneous multi-channel EEG, and a 2-channel EEG  tests.
Participants with normal hearing will take part in a one-time session involving tone audiometry, simultaneous multi-channel EEG, and a 2-channel EEG tests.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Implanted with a CI
Exclusion criteria:
Under 18 years of age, native language not German, Neurological Disorders
